added_lines: samaritans: 116 123 free. update from victoria i had a text message recently from fr dean in victoria, to tell me that he was exhausted. apparently some initiatives in the cathedral parish (where i spent my sabbatical) succeeded beyond the staff’s wildest dreams. in september, they had a volunteers’ fair, to get more helpers on board. cards were left out one week, then the next sunday’s homily encouraged people to sign up. as a result, 75 people volunteered. these had to be vetted and steered to ministries that matched their talents. as a result, the cathedral now has five volunteer gardeners, extra flower arrangers, and numerous stewards and ushers. there’s a lot of work in organising these. last easter vigil, 15 adults were baptised. but 21 have signed up for baptism in 2027, and 19 adults seek confirmation. all 40 meet each week and learn about the catholc faith. more work for fr dean: even reporting this sounds exhausting. fr dean also reported that the youngest of his five sons has mental health issues that have brought him to hospital and caused fr dean and his wife linda endless worry. if you have a spare prayer, please remember them, and their son, as will i. fr bernard the parish office is closed until monday november 2. point to ponder : the catholic faith is built on belonging to a shared family of faith rather than walking alone. faith requires tangible loving actions rather than just passive thoughts. aughadown

thirtieth sunday in ordinary time the pharisees fault was not gratitude for doing good hut contempt for those less successful, a lack of humility before the grace of god. paul too could ‘boast’ and give thanks that he had kept the faith, but he recognised that this had not been simply his own doing but because ‘the lord stood by me.’ we too should thank god for any good we have been able to do. it is with his help that we do it, and it gives us no grounds for complacency or a sense of superiority. the parishioner ‘love one another as i have loved you’sunday 25-october-2026 i love you, lord, my strength. visit our website: theparishioner.ie or facebook

removed_lines: saint of the week poor jude must be worn out in heaven.
as the patron saint of hopeless cases, his help is sought by countless people.
why has jude been given the care of difficult situations?
some think it may be because of confusion between his name and that of judas iscariot, the traitor.
as a result, people may have thought there was no point in praying to him: it was hopeless.

all we know is that jude was an apostle and martyr, honoured with st simon each year on 28 october. (from ‘scandalous saints and spirited sinners’, veritas publications 2005, by bernard cotter) family of parishes office to book masses, arrange weddings, baptisms, anniversaries, etc.

samaritans: 116 123 free. update from victoria i had a text message recently from fr dean in victoria, to tell me that he was exhausted.
apparently some initiatives in the cathedral parish (where i spent my sabbatical) succeeded beyond the staff’s wildest dreams. in september, they had a volunteers’ fair, to get more helpers on board.
cards were left out one week, then the next sunday’s homily encouraged people to sign up.
as a result, 75 people volunteered. these had to be vetted and steered to ministries that matched their talents.
as a result, the cathedral now has five volunteer gardeners, extra flower arrangers, and numerous stewards and ushers.
there’s a lot of work in organising these.
last easter vigil, 15 adults were baptised.
but 21 have signed up for baptism in 2027, and 19 adults seek confirmation.
all 40 meet each week and learn about the catholc faith.
more work for fr dean: even reporting this sounds exhausting.
fr dean also reported that the youngest of his five sons has mental health issues that have brought him to hospital and caused fr dean and his wife linda endless worry.

if you have a spare prayer, please remember them, and their son, as will i. fr bernard the parish office is closed until monday november 2. point to ponder : the catholic faith is built on belonging to a shared family of faith rather than walking alone.
faith requires tangible loving actions rather than just passive thoughts.
